units.titles: Native tokens from the L1 liquidity pools could be drained depending on the compiler version used | DiscretionaryExitFee can be drained
units.known_address_notes: Audit scope is Boba's L1LiquidityPool.sol / L1LiquidityPoolAltL1.sol. Boba's own mainnet address book lists L1LiquidityPool=0x3d95bE... and Proxy__L1LiquidityPool=0x1A26ef..., both verified on Ethereum as L1LiquidityPool; the live proxy implementation() is 0xd244... (solc 0.8.9). AltL1 variant is not in the Ethereum address book (deployed on other chains), so only the Ethereum L1 pool is asserted.

units.titles: Lack of PDA check on TWTM leads to user wallet account draining | Same pool holding swaps allow unbacked SOLS minting
units.known_address_notes: Corpus-supplied program id confirmed live and executable. Sanctum's own 'Deployed programs' page lists 5ocnV1qiCgaQR8Jb8xWnVbApfaygJ8tNoZfgPwsgx9kx as 'S Controller', the program that mints/burns SOLS and holds the pool/holding logic described in the report (EndRebal, SVC program, holding accounts). Program is upgradeable (BPFLoaderUpgradeab1e), so the deployed build may post-date the audited commit -> address is the exact live instance of the audited program.
